chapter: Precision, the union and learning to read
title: The band's spontaneous stage show and glee club
summary: Crawford describes trumpets and trombones thrown and caught, saxophones promenading, and the choral arrangements Sy Oliver began.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And you said the band was a very exciting band, too, you said the guys --
Oh, yeah. They put on a show for them.
Did you all work that out before you went out to play?
No, things just going, things just started happening. Trumpeters would throw their trumpets in the air, all at the same time, simultaneously. Is this on?
And they'd catch them. And they would change mutes at the same time. Everything was precise.
And these things were spontaneous. They happened on the bandstand.
Spontaneous, spontaneous. Eddie Durham brought a trick in there, where you throw your trombone and all of a sudden you just let it go, and slide --
Almost off, but for some reason, he had the knack of catching it and his hands was back here, right-handed or left-handed, and would catch it just before it would

fall. So we had the trombones doing that. Saxophones -- well, they used to promenade around, in and out of the wings, in and out of the bandstand, blowing, still blowing. Just the rhythm stayed on the stage.
We had a glee club that really sang.
Oh, that's right because you all did those choral arrangements, too, that were in the band.
Yes, sir. Sy Oliver started that. He was very much an instigator, and shaping that band. That's all I got to say about him.

Yeah, well, I think that had a -- because I know I've heard Ellington recording in which it seems as though they had heard -- Duke had heard that, there was a record called 'I Just Got To Be A Rug Cutter.' And Harry Carney and a couple of the other guys in the band are singing harmony.

Yeah, well, they got it from us. I won't say that's a true statement, but they were inspired by that Lunceford band. Man, we put on a show. And it was done simultaneously, just automatically created while he were playing. Now, we did rehearse the choral group, oh, yes, had to rehearse that. That was like playing.
I'm getting a little tired, now.
